svg.text: Vomiting blood: what is actually happening
Two very different bleeds
Ulcer bleed
Arterial ooze from an eroded ulcer base.
Often a history of epigastric pain or of
anti-inflammatory tablets bought over the counter.
Variceal bleed
Swollen veins at the lower oesophagus, caused by
back-pressure from a scarred liver. Look for
jaundice, ascites, spider naevi, known cirrhosis.
Priorities are the same for both
Airway first — a patient vomiting blood while
drowsy will aspirate. Position on the side.
Two large cannulae, group and cross-match,
fluids now, blood when available.
Nil by mouth. Hourly pulse, blood pressure,
conscious level and urine output.
Endoscopy is both the diagnosis and the
treatment — the nurse prepares for it early.
The blood pressure lies, and the pulse tells the truth first
A young adult can lose a litre and a half of blood with a blood pressure that is still normal, because the body
clamps down the vessels to protect it. What changes early is the pulse rising, the hands going cool, and the
patient becoming anxious or restless. By the time the pressure falls, compensation has already failed.
Black stool is not a separate problem
Tarry black stool with a foul smell is digested blood from higher up the gut. It means the bleeding has already
happened, even if nothing has been vomited. Iron tablets also darken the stool, but that stool is formed and
not sticky, and the patient is not shocked. When in doubt, treat it as a bleed and check the observations.
